approach.method_basis: The Parent is a graph-based genetic algorithm for molecules. Posterior sampling, in the style of Thompson sampling, decides which offspring get evaluated. Each round it keeps the 64 best scored molecules and draws parents mostly from the top-ranked quantiles. From them it breeds a fresh candidate pool sixteen times the batch size. About 45% of candidates join connected fragments of two scored parents, sometimes followed by one finishing edit. The rest come from a short random walk of atom, bond and ring edits on a single parent. The walk is one edit with probability 0.82, two with 0.15 and three with 0.03. It is lengthened further only when the pool fills very slowly, which has not happened in practice. Every candidate must be a valid, previously unseen canonical molecule. It must also pass a narrow sulfur check that rejects offspring carrying an unusual sulfur environment that none of their scored parents had. A Gaussian process is then fitted only to this task's scored molecules, using count-based Morgan fingerprints and a generalized Tanimoto kernel. It draws one correlated posterior sample per batch slot and takes the highest-sampled remaining candidate. Earlier Children disabled direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen swaps and added the sulfur check.
approach.novelty: This Child removes one thing: the optional second and third edits of the single-parent random walk. Every ordinary mutation offspring is now exactly one edit away from its parent: one bounded edit attempt, with its usual internal retries. The random draw that used to pick the walk length is still made, so the random stream matches the Parent up to the first shortened walk. Crossover, its finishing edit, the slow-pool lengthening rule, the sulfur check, the pool size and the posterior selector are all unchanged. This is a contribution probe, not an attempted improvement. It asks whether multi-edit jumps help on this particular Parent. The same removal cost 0.027 and 0.019 on two earlier Parents, and a model-guided version of the extra edits cost 0.048. None of these was measured with the sulfur check, which rejects multi-edit products more often than other products. The other Children in this round change the surrogate's kernel or enlarge the candidate pool. None of them changes how far an offspring moves from its parent.

observed_bottleneck: On the current sulfur-gated Parent n-1744a1494180 the ordinary single-parent walk takes a sampled second or third mutate call in about 18% of attempts, always at saturation floor one. Re-derived from its 15 actual task logs: 7,502 of 41,688 ordinary attempts make 8,742 second/third calls (6,262 two-call and 1,240 three-call walks; 448-551 multi-call attempts in every task/seed session); no pooled member ever needed more than six attempts, so the floor>1 recovery path (80 attempts) never ran. These walks make larger jumps: evaluated two-/three-edit ordinary offspring have binary Morgan Tanimoto 0.583/0.492 to their generating parent versus 0.729 for one-edit offspring. They supply 310 of 4,350 evaluated offspring with 43 parent beats, 16 incumbent improvements and 144 later breeding uses. Descriptively, 12 of 15 final bests, including the late deco_hop seed-0 0.8561 endpoint, have a multi-edit product somewhere in their accepted ancestry. This ancestry is pervasive (2,703 of 4,350 accepted) and is not causal evidence. The sulfur gate that this Parent added rejects multi-edit products disproportionately: 38 of its 130 rejections come from roughly 10% of breeding attempts. The contribution of this continuation on this Parent is unmeasured. The frozen catalog marks m-00000000000b needs_evidence here because its isolated removals were measured only on other Parents: -0.026868 for n-dbee08307e86 on the ungated count-GP Parent n-62daf219c70a, and -0.019180 for n-29d770e728a6 on an exchange-containing Parent. The guided-continuation modification n-87c89dda7e3b (-0.048083) was also measured on another Parent. Removing crossover (n-767d2ce08797, -0.054937) shows that the single-parent walk is the other main generator route, so its multi-edit component is the next uncovered generator contribution.
hypothesis: Remove optional ordinary single-parent mutation continuation (m-00000000000b). When the inherited saturation floor min(6, 1 + member_attempts // 80) equals one, each ordinary single-parent breeding attempt makes exactly one GraphOperators.mutate call. The original base-length draw rng.choices([1, 2, 3], [0.82, 0.15, 0.03]) is still made at its original position. When the floor exceeds one, the inherited max(base length, floor) walk is kept. Crossover and its finishing mutation, mutate's internal retries, the sulfur admission gate, pool size and correlated posterior allocation are unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Removing multi-edit mutation walks costs 0.031 on the sulfur-gated Parent; all three seeds fall, so ordinary continuation helps here too
finding_summary.insights: Optional multi-edit continuation now has a positive contribution on three different Parents: -0.027 on the ungated count-GP Parent, -0.019 on an exchange-containing Parent, and -0.031 here. The sulfur gate, which rejects multi-edit products disproportionately, did not change the sign, so the gap the catalog flagged for this Anchor is closed: keep continuation. The loss does not appear in local hit rates. Parent-beating offspring (648 to 659) and incumbent improvements (255 to 277) were flat or slightly up, and the single-edit products of formerly long requests were at least as productive per evaluation as the multi-edit ones they replaced (95 parent beats in 525 evaluations, against 43 in 310). So the value of the occasional two- or three-edit jump is not a higher success rate per proposal. It lies in the rarer larger moves that set where a run ends up: plateau escapes, late breakthroughs and the zaleplon winner that only a two-edit walk produced. That matches the Molecular assessment: without continuation, late leaders are one-atom permutations of a single inherited core, the 'refining familiar structures' pattern the research brief worries about, now somewhat stronger. Three cautions narrow the reading. First, about half the similarity gain comes from one-edit offspring themselves sitting closer to their parents in the diverged populations, not only from fewer long walks. Second, the uniform sitagliptin loss occurs where the Parent's multi-edit products never improved the incumbent, so part of the effect is adaptive divergence whose mechanism is unidentified. Third, sulfur-gate rejection counts track population chemistry rather than walk length, so they are a poor activation proxy. Worth trying next: a modestly larger or adaptive multi-edit share, testing the opposite direction. This removal does not locate an optimum, and the model-guided continuation variant lost 0.048 elsewhere, so more steps are not automatically better. Higher-floor saturation recovery and interactions with this round's kernel and pool-size siblings remain untested.
finding_summary.results: The removal ran exactly as intended. In all 15 task/seed runs every ordinary single-parent mutation made one edit, suppressing 8,726 requested second and third edits; the Parent had made 8,742. About 18% of requests (7,463 of 41,716) asked for a longer walk and were cut to one edit, so the removal was exposed in every run. Before the first cut, each run reproduced the Parent molecule for molecule. No multi-edit offspring reached a pool or the oracle; the Parent evaluated 310 of them. Evaluated mutation offspring moved closer to their parents: mean Tanimoto similarity rose from 0.712 to 0.746, and the share below 0.5 fell from 6.2% to 1.9%. Crossover finishing (0.358), mutate retries, full 160-member pools and every posterior fit and selection were unchanged. One prediction failed. Ordinary sulfur-gate rejections were expected to fall below 100 but rose from 100 to 232. Multi-edit rejections did fall from 38 to zero, and the gate rule held in every case. Most of the rise (197 of 295 rejections) came from drd2, where the Child's populations drifted onto sulfur-bearing scaffolds: 97-99% of parents, against 21-41% in the Parent. The mean score fell from 0.5965 to 0.5658 (-0.0307), well past the 0.002 scale, and all three seeds were lower (-0.070, -0.007, -0.015). Nine of 15 task/seed cells were lower, four higher and two within the band. The largest single loss was deco_hop seed 0: the Parent's late 0.856 breakthrough was not reproduced and the Child ended at 0.607, accounting for -0.017 of the mean. Without that cell the loss is still -0.014. zaleplon was lower in all three seeds (-0.012 to -0.024), and in seed 1 the Parent's winning molecule was itself a two-edit product. sitagliptin was lower in all three seeds (-0.032 to -0.088). median_2 was slightly higher in all three (+0.001 to +0.025), and drd2 was mixed.

molecular.headline: Heavily halogenated, ring-dense aromatic decorations of one inherited core per seed; no stereochemistry, no ionizable centres, and many one-atom leader variants
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives this node emits small-to-medium, strongly ring-bearing, strongly aromatic graphs: digest ring_closure_rate runs 0.969-0.985 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.952-0.977 on every task, over 870 optimizer proposals per task from 900 reads. Mean SMILES length is 42-87 characters, so these are ordinary-sized organic molecules, not oligomers. What the molecules consistently are is a single inherited polycyclic core carried from the initial pool, decorated by single-atom and single-substituent swaps: the top of each seed's run is a family of near-identical strings differing in one terminal atom. What they consistently are not is stereochemically defined (stereocentre_rate is exactly 0.0 on all five tasks despite many sp3 ring junctions and alpha-branched carbons in the emitted graphs), ionizable (charged_rate is exactly 0.0 everywhere), or free of heteroatom-bound halogen. Halogen content is extreme on three objectives (halogen_rate 0.886, 0.985 and 0.725) and most of it is decorative rather than structural: fluorine, chlorine and bromine sit on amide nitrogens, on ring nitrogens and on benzylic carbons as the cheapest available edit. The search also spends real evaluations on degenerate one- to three-heavy-atom fragments (C, Cl, FCl, ClBr, SS, FF, CO, C=C, C#C) that score at or near the floor of their task. Relative to the Parent's trajectories under the same seeds and the same 300-evaluation budget, this node's molecules are larger and ring-richer on the decoy-rich objectives and show more alkyl-halide and hydrazide-type edits, but its leader families are flatter: the final-stretch molecules are one-atom permutations of the incumbent rather than new scaffolds.

per_task.generated_character: Compact bicyclic heteroaromatics, mean SMILES length 42.2 and max 74, essentially all ring-bearing (ring_closure_rate 0.970) and aromatic (0.969). The dominant family is an indole-2-carboxamide: an N-H indole or N-methyl indole bearing a carboxamide to a second aryl or pyridyl ring, with methyl, methoxy and halomethyl decoration on the carbocyclic edge, as in Cc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(NCl)c3cccc(O)c3)cc2c(C)c1CBr. One seed instead carries a cyclobuta-fused indole, COc1cc2c(cc(C(=O)c3ccc(CF)nc3)n2C)c2c1CC2. Halogen content is very high (halogen_rate 0.886) and almost all of it is terminal F, Cl or Br on a methyl or on the amide nitrogen. No stereocentres and no charges are written anywhere (both rates 0.0).
liabilities: N-halogen and N-amino amide nitrogens (N(NCl), N(N)) in the single highest-scoring family
benzylic bromide and chloride as the main score-carrying substituent
degenerate diatomic proposals such as FCl and ClBr consume evaluations at score 0.0
late-run molecules drift off the aromatic core into non-aromatic C=C ring forms that lose score
missing_features: no basic amine centre anywhere in the leader family, so no ionizable head group
no sulfonamide, nitrile, or other polar acceptor beyond the single amide carbonyl
no saturated ring appended to the aromatic core; fused rings are inherited, never built
no defined stereochemistry on the sp3 carbons it does make
no fused five/six heteroaromatic alternatives to the inherited indole; the core never changes within a seed
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The run starts from an initial indole carboxamide at 0.305 and the whole gradient to the 0.450 best is terminal decoration: swapping the two methoxy groups of COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC for methyl plus halomethyl, adding a meta-phenol, and substituting the amide nitrogen. The three molecules at exactly 0.44990 differ only in which halogen sits on one benzylic carbon, which says the objective is nearly flat in that substituent and the optimizer is buying its last gains from a feature the score barely distinguishes. Everything that loses score loses the bicycle: the 0.0 molecules are FCl, ClBr, Cl and C.

per_task.generated_character: By far the largest molecules of the panel: mean SMILES length 86.5, max 217, ring_closure_rate 0.978 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.977. The leaders are fused bicyclic azine cores, a pyrimidine or triazolo-fused ring system, carrying a second heteroaryl ring through an N-aryl bond and then loaded with long conjugated open chains, as in C#CC(Cl)(C(=C)C)n1c(=O)c(=CC)c(=CNc2nc(C)nc3c(C=O)c(C)ccc23)n(-c2nc(C)nc(=CC)c2=CC(C)C=C)c1=O. Later molecules converge on a thiomethyl-substituted polycyclic system, C=CC(=CC)c1c2c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n(C)c2nn1-c1cc2c(=O)c3c4nnnc3c(c1SC)c2o4. A noticeable fraction carries exocyclic methylidene and formyl groups on what should be aromatic positions, which is why cumulated_double_bond_rate is non-zero (0.0057) here.
liabilities: exocyclic methylidene and imine substituents written onto aromatic ring atoms, giving cross-conjugated systems a chemist would not draw
long polyene and enyne chains hung off the core that add mass but no recognizable pharmacophore
terminal alkyne plus tertiary chloride on the same quaternary carbon in the top-scoring molecule
one- and two-atom fragments still evaluated at the 0.5 floor, wasting budget
missing_features: no compact, well-formed linker between the two ring systems; the connection is a bare N-aryl bond
no sulfonamide, sulfone or other polar connector chemistry at the decoration point
no saturated or partially saturated ring appended as a side decoration
no stereochemistry anywhere, despite many sp3 branch points in the chains
no ionizable group; charged_rate is 0.0 across the whole set
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Every initial molecule already scores about 0.50-0.55 and the floor of the whole task is 0.5, which the trivial fragments Cl, C, CBr, CCl, CC=CSC and C#CF all hit. Score above that is bought by assembling more fused ring systems and more heteroaryl-to-heteroaryl linkages onto one core, and the 0.638 best is simply the most elaborate version of that core. Nothing in the gradient rewards trimming: the molecules get monotonically heavier and less drug-like as the score rises.

per_task.generated_character: Mid-sized molecules, mean SMILES length 59.2, ring_closure_rate 0.975, aromatic_atom_rate 0.970 and the highest halogen_rate on the panel at 0.985. This is the one objective where the leaders carry a genuine basic amine on a ring: pyrrolidine, piperidine, tetrahydropyridine and imidazolidine nitrogens appear throughout, for example COc1cc(C(=CBr)N2CCCNC2N)c(N)c(CCc2cccc(Cl)c2)c1S and CCCc1cc(C2=CCN(C)CC2)c(N)c(CCc2cccc(Cl)c2)c1S. The other leader family pairs a saturated diamine ring with an aryl sulfinyl group, CCN(CC1Cc2cc(Br)cc(OC)c21)C1CNCN1S(=O)c1cccc(Cl)c1N. Chlorinated and brominated anilines are everywhere; thiol and thioether sulfur recurs on the aromatic ring.
liabilities: free aromatic thiol and thioether sulfur on the top-scoring cores
aminal N-C-N motifs inside the saturated ring of the leading family
sulfinyl rather than sulfonyl sulfur as the leaders' connecting group
O-O peroxide linkage written into one high-scoring molecule, CCN(CC1CCc2cc(Br)cc(OO)c21)C1CNCN1S(=O)c1cccc(Cl)c1N
trisubstituted aniline carrying both an amine and a thiol on the same ring
missing_features: no clean two- or three-carbon alkyl linker between the basic amine and the distal aromatic ring; the connection is usually direct
no amide or ether tether in the high-scoring family, so the chemotype is held together by C-C and C-N bonds only
no stereochemistry written on the saturated ring carbons that carry the basic nitrogen
no salt or protonated form represented; charged_rate is 0.0
no conventional sulfone or sulfonamide retained among the leaders
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The low end is the inherited arylsulfonyl proline amide, CNC(=O)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 at 0.00026, and its fragments, O=S(=O)(Cl)c1cc(Cl)cc(CCl)c1 and Cc1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 near 0.0004-0.002. Score climbs to 0.99 once a saturated nitrogen ring is attached to an electron-rich aniline-bearing aromatic ring with a lipophilic chloroaryl tail: that combination of basic nitrogen, aromatic amine and halogenated distal ring is what the gradient rewards. The sulfonamide is converted to a sulfinyl on the way up, which trades a well-formed group for a less conventional one while the score rises.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length 59.1, ring_closure_rate 0.985, aromatic_atom_rate 0.982 and the lowest halogen_rate of the panel at 0.110, so this is the one objective where the generator decorates with carbon and nitrogen rather than halogen. The leader family is a single elaborate polycyclic cage: a 3-propyl-2-ethoxy quinoline fused through a spiro centre into a benzoxazine and then into a piperazinone, CCCc1nc2ccccc2c(C23NOc4ccc(cc42)C2C(=O)C34CCN(C)CCN4C(=O)N2C)c1OCC. Nearly every top molecule is the same cage with one ring atom exchanged: N-O for N-C-O, an extra O, an S in place of N. One seed ends on an open macrocyclic lactam version, CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(N2C3=C(C)C(=O)NN(C)CC(=O)N(C)CCCC2(S)c2ccccc23)c1.
liabilities: N-O and O-O bonds written directly into the ring skeleton of the leading cage
spiro and bridged ring junctions assembled with no stereochemical specification at all
a free thiol placed on a quaternary ring carbon in the late molecules
single-atom proposals such as CO and OO evaluated at the task floor
missing_features: no second distinct scaffold explored; the leaders are one cage with atom substitutions
no simple bicyclic or monocyclic alternative tested at the top of the run
no stereochemistry on a cage with multiple genuine ring-fusion and spiro centres
no carboxylic acid, sulfonamide or other strong polar handle
no aromatic ring added beyond the two inherited ones
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Scores are compressed: the best is 0.246, the median 0.201, and almost all optimizer molecules sit in a narrow band, so the gradient gives the search very little to climb. What separates 0.246 from 0.235 is a single ring heteroatom swap inside the cage, not any chemical idea. The floor is reached only by fragments: C=C, C#C, C, OO at 0.0 and CO at 0.0088. The run therefore spends its budget permuting one inherited cage rather than finding a second chemotype.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length 50.0, ring_closure_rate 0.969, aromatic_atom_rate 0.952, halogen_rate 0.725 and the highest cumulated_double_bond_rate of the panel at 0.032. Two families dominate. One is an amidine or guanidine-bearing cyclohexadiene or phenyl ring fused to a bicyclic urea, N=C(NCF)C1=CCC(N2C(c3ccccn3)=C3C(=O)N(F)CN(F)C32)=C1. The other is a methylated purine-like core N-linked to a cyclopentadiene carrying an imidoyl fluoride, CC1=C=C=C(C(=N)F)C1(CF)n1cc2c(c1C)c(=N)n(C)c(=O)n2F. Fluorine is placed on nitrogen as often as on carbon, and the imine/amidine C=N appears in most leaders.
liabilities: N-F bonds on amide and ring nitrogens throughout the top molecules
imidoyl fluoride C(=N)F groups carried by most leaders
cumulated C=C=C units inside a five-membered ring, as in CC1=C=C=C(C(=N)F)C1(CF)n1cc2c(c1C)c(=N)n(C)c(=O)n2F
free thiol substituents on quaternary ring carbons
diatomic proposals FF and SS evaluated at the numerical floor
missing_features: no beta-amino amide motif; the amine-to-carbonyl relationship that defines this chemotype never forms
no defined stereochemistry at all, on an objective whose reference chemotype is a single enantiomer
no trifluoromethyl or aryl-CF3 group; fluorine is placed one atom at a time, often on nitrogen
no saturated piperazine or fused triazolopiperazine partner ring
no neutral primary amine on an sp3 carbon in the leading families
per_task.score_gradient_reading: All ten initial molecules score between 1e-27 and 2.5e-05, so almost any ring-bearing fluorinated amidine is an enormous improvement, and the gradient from there to 0.606 is driven by packing fluorine and C=N onto a small bicyclic nitrogen heterocycle. The floor molecules are diatomics, FF, SS, C#CS and CF at 1e-24 to 2e-23, and one large fused molecule at 4e-42, which shows the objective punishes size as hard as it punishes triviality. What the gradient rewards is a small, fluorine-dense, nitrogen-rich ring system; what it does not reward is anything the generator can build cleanly.

transferable_gaps.evidence: N-F and N-Cl bonds on amide and ring nitrogens appear in the highest-scoring molecules of three of the five objectives, for example Cc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(NCl)c3cccc(O)c3)cc2c(C)c1CBr and N=C(NCF)C1=CCC(N2C(c3ccccn3)=C3C(=O)N(F)CN(F)C32)=C1, and O-halogen and S-halogen variants also occur. Digest halogen_rate is 0.886, 0.985 and 0.725 on three objectives, so halogen placement is the generator's dominant decoration channel, not a rare accident.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator attaches halogens to heteroatoms as freely as to carbon, so an edit a chemist would reject is one of its cheapest and most-used moves.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Restrict halogen substitution to carbon attachment points, and give the operator a carbon-attached replacement for every heteroatom-attached halogen it would otherwise place, so the same amount of local exploration is kept without emitting bonds that are chemically indefensible.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On every objective the top molecules within one seed share an identical core and differ in one terminal atom: Cc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(NCl)c3cccc(O)c3)cc2c(C)c1CBr and Cc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)N(NCl)c3cccc(O)c3)cc2c(C)c1CCl score identically at 0.44990, and CCCc1nc2ccccc2c(C23NOc4ccc(cc42)C2C(=O)C34CCN(C)CCN4C(=O)N2C)c1OCC versus CCCc1nc2ccccc2c(C23NOOc4ccc(cc42)C2C(=O)C34CCN(C)CCN4C(=O)N2C)c1OCC differ by one inserted ring oxygen.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot build or replace a ring system; it only substitutes atoms on a scaffold it inherited from the initial pool.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add scaffold-level moves that exchange one ring system for another of comparable size while preserving the existing substituents and their attachment vectors, so late search can leave a plateau instead of permuting terminal atoms on a fixed core.

transferable_gaps.evidence: stereocentre_rate is exactly 0.0 in all five digest counter blocks over 870 proposals each, while the molecules themselves carry genuine sp3 centres: the spiro and ring-fusion carbons of CCCc1nc2ccccc2c(C23NOc4ccc(cc42)C2C(=O)C34CCN(C)CCN4C(=O)N2C)c1OCC and the saturated diamine ring of CCN(CC1Cc2cc(Br)cc(OC)c21)C1CNCN1S(=O)c1cccc(Cl)c1N are all written flat.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator writes no stereochemistry, even when it constructs ring fusions, spiro centres and alpha-branched carbons that have defined configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Carry and resolve configuration through mutation and crossover so that a produced molecule is a specific compound rather than a configurational family, and treat achiral or configurationally unstable centres explicitly instead of omitting all of them.

transferable_gaps.evidence: charged_rate is exactly 0.0 on all five objectives. Where a basic nitrogen does appear it is drawn neutral, as in CCCc1cc(C2=CCN(C)CC2)c(N)c(CCc2cccc(Cl)c2)c1S, and no carboxylate, ammonium or counterion form occurs anywhere in the digest.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces no ionizable or charged species; the whole output is neutral closed-shell notation with no acid or protonated base represented.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Let the candidate chemistry include ionizable groups and represent their relevant protonation state, so that polarity and charge are explorable variables rather than a fixed property of the representation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Fragments such as FCl, ClBr, SS, FF, C#CS, CO, OO, C#C and CC=CSC appear as worst-case entries on every objective, at 0.0, at the task floor of 0.5, or at 1e-24 to 1e-23, and some of them occur as late as evaluation 287 and 292 of a 300-evaluation budget.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator regularly emits one- to three-heavy-atom fragments and evaluates them, spending oracle budget on molecules that cannot score.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make deletion and fragmentation operators size-aware so an edit that strips a molecule below a minimum heavy-atom count is repaired or re-drawn before it consumes an evaluation, rather than being emitted and scored.

transferable_gaps.evidence: cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.032 and 0.0057 on two objectives, and the pattern reaches the leaders: CC1=C=C=C(C(=N)F)C1(CF)n1cc2c(c1C)c(=N)n(C)c(=O)n2F places a C=C=C unit inside a five-membered ring, and C#CC(Cl)(C(=C)C)n1c(=O)c(=CC)c(=CNc2nc(C)nc3c(C=O)c(C)ccc23)n(-c2nc(C)nc(=CC)c2=CC(C)C=C)c1=O hangs exocyclic methylidenes off ring atoms of an aromatic system.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator creates strained and cross-conjugated unsaturation it cannot distinguish from ordinary unsaturation: cumulated double bonds and exocyclic methylidenes on aromatic ring atoms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Bond-order and ring-unsaturation operators need geometric feasibility checks tied to ring size and to the aromatic state of the atom being modified, with a feasible alternative offered rather than the edit simply being allowed through.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The final six molecules of one run are all the same bicyclic cage with one atom changed, and in another the final molecules C=COc1c(NC)cc2c(c1C)C=C2C(=O)NN(F)c1ccccc1, C=COc1c(NC)cc2c(c1C)C=C2C(=O)Oc1ccccn1 and C=COc1c(NC)cc2c(c1C)C=C2C(=O)NOc1cccnn1 share one core and differ only in the linker atom between carbonyl and aryl ring.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator's late-run output collapses to one motif per run, so the molecules it reports at the end carry no second hypothesis.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Keep structurally distinct families alive in the breeding population rather than letting the pool converge on the incumbent's neighbourhood, so that the end of a run holds more than one chemotype.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A well-formed arylsulfonyl amide exists in the initial pool, CNC(=O)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1, and the high-scoring descendants replace it with a sulfinyl, as in CCN(CC1Cc2cc(Br)cc(OC)c21)C1CNCN1S(=O)c1cccc(Cl)c1N; elsewhere the connectors that survive are N-N, N-O and S-H, for example CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(N2C3=C(C)C(=O)NN(C)CC(=O)N(C)CCCC2(S)c2ccccc23)c1.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator rarely forms the conventional polar connectors of medicinal chemistry, and when one is inherited it is more likely to be degraded than elaborated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Give the operator set group-level edits that build intact sulfonamide, ether, ester and amide connectors as units, instead of reaching those regions only through atom-at-a-time changes that pass through unstable intermediates and settle there.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
